public_rationale: The PEACH trial report, published July 21, 2025, found no significant overall reduction in documentation time, although some subgroups saved time [e1]. Its economic model projected annual institutional savings of SGD197,501; it did not measure realized annual savings [e1]. These results do not establish realized net benefits attributable to improved model capabilities, or establish that no participant benefits economically [e1].
limitations: Projected savings do not establish realized benefits after all relevant costs.
The trial does not isolate the economic contribution of improvements between model versions.
One clinical deployment cannot establish costs and benefits for all LLM providers and users.
The claim specifies no starting model or baseline date.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs have improved, but not in a way that makes economic sense for anyone involved.

statement.excerpt: LLMs have gotten “better,” but the “better” is not the kind of “better” that actually makes “economic sense for literally anyone involved.”

from_speaker: economic sense for literally anyone involved
our_interpretation: Read 'have gotten better' as accumulated improvement through the post date. No starting date is supplied.
The ordinary economic reading is that benefits justify relevant acquisition, deployment, oversight, and use costs for at least one participant.
A customer can benefit even if a model provider loses money. The claim covers both.
This is a general economic-benefit claim, not a stated financial metric for a named company; metric_scope is therefore null.
Productivity gains, projected savings, and consumer valuations are relevant but do not automatically establish realized net financial benefits attributable to model improvements.
criteria.support_condition: Broad, credible cost-benefit evidence establishes that improved LLM capabilities have produced no economically worthwhile use for any covered participant.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one credible case establishes benefits exceeding relevant costs for a provider or user because of improved LLM capabilities.

evidence.explanation: The randomized trial found no significant overall documentation-time reduction, although some subgroups improved. Its favorable financial result is an annual savings projection, not a measurement of realized net savings or the incremental value of a newer model.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: For the period through August 25, 2026, document realized benefits attributable to improved LLM capabilities against a clear baseline. Include acquisition, deployment, operating and oversight costs. One credible case where benefits exceeded those costs would contradict the claim. Support would require broad evidence establishing that no covered participant had an economically worthwhile use.
